note.note:
History:
- 25-30 yo female (exact age not stated) presents with an acute, severe, throbbing headache on the left side that began “mid-day” today (≈ few hours ago).
- Preceded by visual aura described as “zig-zag lines” and blurred vision in both eyes for a few minutes before pain onset.
- Pain is unilateral, throbbing, worsens with leaning forward or moving head/neck.
- Associated symptoms: photophobia (wearing sunglasses indoors), nausea with two episodes of vomiting.
- Denies fever, skin rash, speech difficulties, limb weakness, balance problems, recent head trauma, or breathlessness.
- Similar episode occurred a few weeks ago, lasted ~2 days, improved with rest and over-the-counter analgesics.
- Triggers/Context: High workplace stress; no identified specific triggers yet.

Past Medical History:
- No chronic illnesses reported.
- Family: Mother with migraine and hypothyroidism; no family history of brain tumours.
- Allergies: Not recorded.
- Medications: Microgynon (combined OCP) for contraception, use for 3 months (dose/route/frequency not documented).

Physical Examination:
- General: Patient conversant and oriented; anxious but cooperative.
- Vital signs: Not recorded.
- Neurologic: No reported focal deficits (speech, motor, sensory, coordination); no balance issues.
- HEENT: Photophobia reported; no rash noted.
- Neck: No trauma reported; no documented examination for stiffness.
- Other systems: Not recorded.

Impression:
- Probable migraine with visual aura causing acute unilateral throbbing headache, photophobia, and nausea/vomiting.
  • Alternative considerations (per DDx, lower likelihood but relevant to OCP use and positional worsening): cerebral venous sinus thrombosis; intracranial mass/tumour. No current red-flag features elicited.

Management Plan:
- Symptomatic treatment advised:
  • Analgesia: Paracetamol and/or Co-codamol (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  • NSAID: Ibuprofen or Naproxen if no contraindications (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Headache diary: Record timing, potential triggers, and medication use.
- Education & reassurance: Explained migraine diagnosis; addressed fear of brain cancer.
- Follow-up: Review next week to assess response; consider prophylactic migraine therapy if attacks persist or increase.
- Red-flag advice: Seek immediate care if headache worsens or persists >2-3 days, fails to respond to medications, or if new symptoms arise (neck pain/stiffness, limb weakness, vision changes).

Patient Summary:
Patient with no significant past medical history presents with a second episode of unilateral throbbing headache preceded by visual aura, consistent with migraine with aura. Treated conservatively with analgesia and advised to keep a headache diary; safety-net instructions and follow-up arranged.

Key Takeaways:
- Use recommended analgesics early; combine with an NSAID if needed.
- Keep a detailed headache diary to help identify triggers and guide future therapy.
- Return promptly if headaches escalate, last >2-3 days, or any neurologic or visual changes occur.

Next Steps:
- Re-evaluate in 1 week.
- If headaches recur ≥4 times/month or poorly controlled, discuss prophylactic therapy (e.g., beta-blocker, topiramate) and consider further investigations.
- If red-flag features emerge, arrange urgent neuro-imaging to exclude secondary causes.
